about: The three people who read the player's standing (T165, ADR 0025), each with a fixed manner a designer wrote. A manner is a list of rules read top to bottom; the first that holds sets the person's consequence and greeting, and the last holds always. A rule holds when the world's facts in `when` have their values and the virtue named is at least `at_least`. `sets` is the value of the person's one consequence -- a price in coins, or whether a door opens -- and `says` the greeting. The consequences are standing.json's and only those. A manner never changes, is never saved, and reads only the standing and the world: no deed names a person, and nothing a person says changes what persists.

rules.says: Twice the fare, and pay before you step in.
rules.why: He is afraid of you, and fear is the one thing he charges for.

rules.says: Half fare for you, while the bridge is down.
rules.why: With the bridge down the valley needs his boat, and you have looked after the valley.
With no bread at the market there is nothing to price.

rules.says: Bread is dear today. For you.
rules.why: He overcharges the one he fears, and dares nobody else.

rules.says: A loaf for a coin, friend of the valley.
rules.why: He thanks the one who looks after the valley.

rules.says: The chapel door stays shut to you.
rules.why: She keeps the frightened safe from the one who frightens them.

rules.says: Come in; the chapel is open to you.
rules.why: She opens to the one who has looked after the valley.

rules.says: The chapel opens to those who look after the valley.
rules.why: A stranger has not yet shown what they are.
